job.text: I cannot do it myself, for it is twice as big as I am, but I should think you could lift it easily, now that it is empty." The raccoon threw a perturbed glance at the kettle, and then said in a tone which tried to be nonchalant, "Oh! the kettle is all right. It will get up, I suppose, when it feels like it. If it should ask me to help it, of course I would; but perhaps it may prefer the floor for a change. I--I often lie on the floor, myself," he added. The squirrel stared. "What do you mean?" he said. "It isn't alive! Toto said it wasn't." The raccoon beckoned him aside, and said in a low tone, "My good Cracker, Toto _says_ a great many things, and no doubt he thinks they are all true. But he is a young boy, and, let me tell you, he does _not_ know everything in the world. If that thing is not alive, why did it jump off its seat just at the critical moment, and pour hot water over the robber's legs?" "Did it?" exclaimed the squirrel, much impressed. "Yes,
